title: A schallweg component record
description: One record of the component database: a construction, a lining or a covering. The format, the granularity and the versioning rule are docs/decisions/data-format.md. The fields and what each is for are docs/decisions/element-model.md, which this schema derives from and which says that where the two disagree this schema is what runs. The provenance floor is docs/decisions/certificate-extraction.md. An element and a junction are deliberately not record types here: docs/decisions/element-model.md places an element inside a project rather than in the database, and docs/decisions/junctions.md keys a junction on the identities of elements in a project, so neither can be written down without a project around it.
$comment: Every numeric quantity carries a "unit" annotation naming its SI unit, so a reader of this schema gets the unit from the schema rather than from the spelling of a field name. It is an annotation: a validator ignores it, and it is here because a unit that lives only in a field name cannot be read by anything.

schema.description: The major version of this schema. A record declaring a version this reader does not know is refused rather than read for the fields it recognises, because a major version exists to say those fields may no longer mean what the reader thinks. The rule is docs/decisions/data-format.md. Version 2 is what entering one published report against version 1 forced: five fields changed type or meaning and one was removed, which is a major change under that rule, and the rule also requires every record in the tree to be migrated so that none is left behind at version 1.

id.description: Stable identity, which survives being cited by a result. What makes an identity stable is issue #56.

kind.description: What this record is. It decides which calculations the record may enter and it is not free text.

superseded.description: Values this record used to carry. Append-only, and never a substitute for correcting the current value. The rule and the reason are docs/decisions/data-format.md; the route that makes an entry is issue #78.

basis.description: Whether this construction carries laboratory values or a description. Never inferred from whether the values happen to be present, because an absent spectrum and a description are different statements.

mass_per_area.description: Mass per unit area. Required on every construction, lining and covering: the in situ correction and the junction estimation route both need it and neither can proceed without it.

thickness.description: Total thickness. Derived from the layers where layers are given and stated directly where they are not.

layers.description: The makeup, outermost first. A measured construction whose makeup was not published carries an empty list, and that emptiness is recorded rather than filled with a guess.

airborne_lab.description: The laboratory sound reduction index, band by band. This is what the detailed model runs on.

impact_lab.description: The laboratory normalised impact sound pressure level, band by band. This is what the detailed impact model runs on.

improvement.description: The improvement this lining or covering gives, band by band. A lining carries the airborne improvement and a covering the impact improvement; neither may carry the other's, which is why the quantity is in the value and is constrained by kind below.

airborne_single.description: The weighted sound reduction index and its adaptation terms. This is what the simplified model runs on, and it is not derived from the spectrum by this record nor the spectrum from it: docs/decisions/model-shape.md says the two models each read their own input and neither invents the other's.

impact_single.description: The weighted normalised impact sound pressure level and its adaptation term, for the simplified impact model.

specimen_area.description: Area of the tested specimen. Per record rather than a constant, because a window's specimen is much smaller than a wall's.

specimen_edges.description: The edge lengths of the tested specimen, going round its boundary, so that their sum is its perimeter. A test opening of 4.0 m by 5.0 m is four edges and not two. This replaced a single specimen_edge_length, which asked for one number and did not say which one: either dimension of a rectangular opening, the perimeter, and whatever the in situ correction is referenced to are different numbers, and a record carrying one of them without saying which is a record whose reader has to guess. Any of those can be derived from the edges and none of them can be recovered from a single length, so what the report printed is what is stored and the choice of which combination a correction uses stays with the kernel, where the definition it comes from can be cited.

lab_loss_factor.description: Total loss factor of the specimen as tested. The in situ correction is a correction from this value to the building's, so a laboratory value without it can only be used uncorrected, which is an assumption the result then has to carry.

lab_loss_factor_absent.description: Where the loss factor was looked for and not found, for a record whose report does not print one. It is a sentence rather than a flag so that the absence carries the evidence for itself: which sheets and pages were read, and that none of them stated a loss factor. Version 1 made the loss factor a hard dependency of either laboratory spectrum, and the first published report entered against it did not print one anywhere that was read, so the dependency did not protect the data, it removed it: a certificate that publishes a spectrum and no loss factor could not enter the database at all, and the certificates this project can reach are the published ones. The refusal is replaced by a statement that cannot be omitted. A spectrum entered beside this field is a spectrum that can only be used uncorrected, and it is the result's obligation to carry that, which is what the field makes possible rather than what it decides.

base_construction.description: The construction this improvement was measured on, by identity. Not optional and not a provenance nicety: an improvement measured on a heavy base and applied to a lightweight one is a known way to be several decibels wrong, and nothing downstream can warn about it unless the base is in the record.

allOf.$comment: A construction. Everything except a lining and a covering.

A measured construction carries at least one measured quantity. Which quantities a construction of a given kind needs depends on the calculation it enters, and that is the kernel's refusal to make rather than this schema's: a window with no impact spectrum is complete for its kind, not a record with a field missing.

A described construction carries the makeup and no laboratory values. The first release computes from measured constructions only, and a described one that carried values would be that restriction quietly undone.

A lining improves airborne sound reduction. A covering improves impact sound transmission. They enter the calculation at different points, and a record that could carry either quantity would let one be applied where the other belongs.

A laboratory spectrum without the specimen it was measured on cannot be corrected to a building, and a record carrying one without the others is the case that produces an uncorrected number nobody notices.

The loss factor is either stated or its absence is. oneOf rather than anyOf, so a record cannot carry both a value and a statement that there is none, which would leave a reader with two answers and no rule for choosing between them.
A measured record's provenance has to reach the certificate floor. A described one has no certificate, so it reaches the smaller floor of who wrote it down and where the description came from.

A rating that this record carries names the standard it was rated to. The measurement standard and the rating standard are different documents with different editions, and version 1 had one field for both, so a record could state a rating whose procedure nobody can identify.
The same obligation for a measured spectrum, against the measurement standard rather than the rating one.

identifier.description: An identity used to cite a record from another record or from a result. Lower case, digits and hyphens, so that two spellings of one identity cannot both exist.

date.description: A calendar date, as year, month and day. No time and no zone: nothing here happens at an hour.

provenance.description: Where this record's values came from. The floor is docs/decisions/certificate-extraction.md, and every field below is there because a record without it either cannot be checked or is not lawfully extractable. Which of these are required depends on whether the record is measured or described, above. What provenance is as a data model, beyond this floor, is issue #74.

laboratory.description: The laboratory that performed the test, by name. A measured value has no meaning apart from who measured it.

report_number.description: The report or certificate number. It is the only way anybody can go and read the original.

test_standards.description: The standards this test was performed and rated to, one field per role. Version 1 had a single test_standard string, and the first report entered against it named five standards, which went in as a sentence: it read well and it defeated the reason the field exists, since the same symbol means different things under different editions and nothing can compare an edition it has to find inside prose.

client.description: The client the test was performed for, usually the manufacturer.

specimen_designation.description: What the report calls the specimen it tested. Every report has one, including a report that tests a construction nobody sells, so this is the field that is always fillable and it is the required one.

product_designation.description: The product as the manufacturer names it, where there is one. It is no longer required. The reason it was is still true, that a user who cannot map a record onto something they can buy cannot use it, but requiring it made the first record enter a laboratory's designation of a test specimen into a field that says product, which presents a construction nobody sells as a product somebody can order. The certificates that are published openly are disproportionately the ones commissioned by associations and public bodies, which test generic constructions, so a required product designation fits the certificates behind a login and not the documents this project can reach. A record without this field is a record of a construction rather than of a product, and that is a fact about the certificate rather than a hole in the record.

obtained_from.description: Where the certificate was obtained, as a citation to the published location. It is the difference between a record extracted from a published document and a record whose origin nobody can state.

described_from.description: For a described construction, where the description came from. It is the same question the certificate citation answers and it has a different answer.

entered_by.description: Who entered the record. Entry from a document is the step where a mistake is invisible: the number is plausible, nothing refuses it, and the only route back is to the person who read the page.

test_standards.description: One standard per role, each with its part and edition as the report prints it. The roles are the ones a report distinguishes: the airborne measurement, the impact measurement, the facility the measurements were made in, and a rating procedure for each of the two quantities. A report that names fewer of them fills fewer fields, and a role nobody read is absent rather than guessed.

airborne.description: The standard the airborne measurement was performed to.

impact.description: The standard the impact measurement was performed to.

facility.description: The standard the test facility itself meets.

airborne_rating.description: The standard the weighted sound reduction index and its adaptation terms were computed to.

impact_rating.description: The standard the weighted impact sound pressure level and its adaptation term were computed to.

superseded.description: One value this record used to carry, with why it stopped being current. A later test is a different fact rather than a correction of the first, and the two forms below are kept apart because collapsing them would make an entry error look like a physical change.

field.description: Which field this entry holds the previous value of.

reason.description: remeasured means a new test exists and the old one was correct for its own test. corrected means the earlier value was entered wrongly from its report.

what_was_wrong.description: For a corrected entry, what was wrong. Required on a correction, because a correction that does not say what it corrects cannot be checked.

layer.description: One part of a construction's makeup. A layer has no acoustic values of its own and is never looked up on its own; it exists so a construction's description is structured rather than a sentence.

material.description: A name from a controlled vocabulary rather than free text, so two records of the same thing are the same thing. The vocabulary itself is not fixed by this schema and is owed by the work that enters the first records.

density.description: Density. A solid is naturally described this way.

mass_per_area.description: Mass per unit area. A sheet is naturally described this way. Forcing one of the two forms would make half the records carry a converted number nobody can check against its source.

attachment.description: How this layer is connected to the one below. This is what distinguishes constructions that are identical on a materials list and tens of decibels apart in practice.

spectrum.description: One entry in every band of a declared band set. There is no route to write a spectrum with a band missing: the band set decides exactly which keys must be present and no others are allowed, which is docs/decisions/frequency-bands.md made a property of the file rather than a convention. The quantity is in the value because a sound reduction index and an impact level are both decibels over the same bands, and a reader that takes one for the other produces a plausible wrong answer. docs/formats/spectrum.md defines R and Ln for the exchange format; the two improvement quantities are record quantities and a record is not an exchange document. An entry is a measured number or a stated bound, and the two are different shapes so that nothing can read one as the other.

quantity.description: R is the sound reduction index, Ln the normalised impact sound pressure level, DR the airborne improvement of a lining, DLn the impact improvement of a covering.

values.description: The entries, keyed by nominal centre frequency in hertz as a string. Nominal rather than exact, because two roundings of one exact frequency would appear as two bands.

band_entry.description: What one band of a spectrum holds: either a number, which is a value that was measured, or a bound, which is a value that was not. A test facility has a limit of its own, and a specimen that out-performs it is reported band by band with a greater-than-or-equal sign against that limit. Version 1 had a plain number per band, so entering such a sheet would have recorded measurements nobody made, invisibly, which is the failure the whole database is arranged against, and the alternative was to enter nothing and lose the certificate. The two shapes are different types rather than a number with a flag beside it, because a reader that has not been written for bounds cannot silently succeed on one: it fails at the point of reading rather than several steps later with a plausible number.

bounded_band_entry.description: A band the test bounds rather than measures. What limited it is required and is a sentence rather than a code, because the thing that limits a measurement is a property of that facility on that day, and a consumer deciding whether the bound is usable needs to read it rather than match it.

bound.description: at_least for a value the specimen is known to reach or exceed, which is what a facility limit gives for a sound reduction index. at_most for the other direction, which is what a background noise limit gives for a level.

value.description: The bound itself, as the report prints it.

limited_by.description: What limited the measurement, as the report states it: the facility's own limit for this test area, the background noise, or whatever else the sheet gives as the reason.

adaptation_terms.description: One adaptation term per band range, keyed by the range it covers, written as the lowest and highest nominal centre frequency in hertz with a hyphen between them. Version 1 held one term with no field saying which range it was for, and the first report entered against it printed four pairs. The key unstated is for the pair a certificate prints on its rating line without naming its range, which is a statement about that document and not about the standard: a reader resolves it from the rating standard the provenance names, and this schema does not resolve it for them, because that would be this repository asserting the content of a standard it does not hold. This is why the ranges are a pattern rather than a list: a list here would be the standard's own table transcribed into a file that cannot cite it.

uncertainty.description: The uncertainty the laboratory states for this rated value, as the report prints it, with the document the figure comes from. It is recorded rather than computed here: it is a fact the certificate asserts, and this project has no route to derive one. It is on the record because a record that asserts a rating with no sign that the laboratory brackets it wider than the margin a user designs to is a record that reads as more precise than its source. What a result prints of it is issue #82 and issue #96, and is a separate question from whether the record can hold it.

value.description: The half-width the report states, so a value of 1.2 means the report brackets the rating by plus or minus 1.2 dB.

source.description: The document the figure comes from, as the report names it.

airborne_rating.description: The weighted sound reduction index with its adaptation terms, as a certificate prints them. The terms are carried beside the rating and never folded into it, because a user who adds them themselves needs to see both.

impact_rating.description: The weighted normalised impact sound pressure level with its adaptation term.
